summary: Backend-only testing for Stripe payment integration completed. All 9 required features verified working. Found and fixed 1 bug in /api/payments/current-plan endpoint (was querying wrong collection for token lookup).
critical_code_review_comments: PASS: POST /api/payments/subscribe creates Stripe checkout session with URL and session_id
PASS: POST /api/payments/subscribe validates plan_id - rejects invalid plans with 400 error
PASS: Valid plan_ids: starter, business, enterprise (custom is contact-sales only)
PASS: GET /api/payments/status/{session_id} returns payment status with plan info
PASS: GET /api/payments/current-plan returns admin's current subscription plan
PASS: POST /api/payments/subscribe stores payment_transactions record in DB
PASS: Health check endpoint returns 200 healthy
PASS: Admin login works with admin/admin123 credentials
FIXED: /api/payments/current-plan was querying admins collection for token - now correctly uses admin_tokens collection
context_for_next_testing_agent: Stripe payment integration fully working. Endpoints: POST /api/payments/subscribe (creates checkout session), GET /api/payments/status/{session_id} (check payment status), GET /api/payments/current-plan?admin_token=X (get current subscription). Plans defined in PLANS dict at line 22-26 of payments.py. Stripe integration uses emergentintegrations library with test key. Transaction records stored in payment_transactions collection.

subscribe_validates_plan_id.evidence: Invalid plan returns 400 {detail: 'Invalid plan'}, custom plan also rejected

subscribe_stores_transaction.evidence: Transaction record created in DB, verified via status endpoint finding the session

admin_login_working.evidence: POST /api/admin/login with admin/admin123 returns token and user info

bugs_fixed.issue: Was querying db.admins.find_one({'token': admin_token}) but tokens are stored in admin_tokens collection
bugs_fixed.fix: Changed to first lookup token in admin_tokens, then find admin by admin_id from token doc

rca_of_the_issue: The current-plan endpoint had a bug where it was looking for the token directly in the admins collection ({token: admin_token}), but the authentication tokens are stored in a separate admin_tokens collection. The fix involves: 1) First looking up the token in admin_tokens to get admin_id, 2) Then querying admins collection by id to get subscription info.
